newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberian commission bars independents from polls.
newsitem.headline: Liberian commission bars independents from polls.

text.p: Liberia's electoral commission has barred independent candidates from May 30 elections intended to end seven years of civil war in the West African nation.

The seven-member independent commission, installed on April 2 after weeks of bickering among Liberia's warring factions over its chairmanship, said in a statement late on Friday that the aim was to ensure stable government.

"The independent election commission therefore wishes to clearly state that only political parties will contest the presidential and legislative elections and not independent candidates," the statement added.
Liberia's West African neighbours brokered the August 1996 peace deal of which the elections are a part.

Their Nigerian-led peacekeeping force ECOMOG supervised disarmament of the rival factions and, while some weapons remain in circulation, its commander, General Victor Malu, gave the poll security clearance in February.
Those running for the presidency include Charles Taylor, the man who launched the war in 1989, and his faction rivals Alhaji Kromah and George Boley.

Freed American slaves founded Liberia in 1847. The war has killed well over 150,000 people and devastated the mining and rubber economy. The latest major flareup in April and May 1996 killed hundreds in the capital.
The commission said three political parties, including Taylor's National Patriotic Party, had registered for the parliamentary poll.
